lines.before: **Terms:** "the owner" = the human who owns the project and locks decisions. "Claude" / "the lead" = the AI session doing the work. "The vault" = the governance `.md` files (tracking files, specs, plans, ADRs), often gitignored. "Tracked" = committed to git.
lines.after: **Terms:** "the owner" = the human who owns the project and locks decisions. "Claude" / "the lead" = the AI session doing the work. "The vault" = the governance `.md` files (tracking files, specs, plans, ADRs), often gitignored. "Tracked" = committed to git. "The owner's yes" = the owner's Yes in a choice pop-up quoting the act exactly. "Outward act" = an act that leaves the machine (push, PR, merge, release, tag, public post, a message out). "The push bound" = the one push that needs no yes (rule:outward-acts). "Gate bypass" = switching a check off (skipping the git hooks, moving the hooks path). "Protected file" = a file only install or the owner writes (the guards, git hooks, .git/config, the settings, the session transcripts).

lines.before: Before the first push, run the strictest check once: `node .claude/first-push-check.mjs`, with the deep sweep (rule:sweep-tiers, first push). It reads every commit's whole tree (merges included) and fails on a kit path, a `never` path, or a secret-shaped file or value in ANY commit, a deleted one included; on an empty `track`, a `track` entry with no tracked file, or a wanted file that is ignored; and on a `never` file sitting unignored in the folder. It lists untracked files to decide. The owner reviews `git ls-files` against the plan. A history hit means rewriting history or a fresh repo, never "delete it in the next commit". The remote is made private first and public only after the owner checks what landed. On a pass the check records the commit; the pre-push hook lets only that commit (or its ancestors and tags) out until it is on a remote branch. **Protect main** once the repo is public and CI has a gate check: copy `.claude/kit/branch-protection.json` to `.kit/`, put the check's name in it (A26), on the owner's go run `gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --input .kit/branch-protection.json`, and read it back; the rule requires that one check, blocks force pushes and deletion, needs no review for a solo owner, and lets admins bypass. `/methodology-kit status` flags an unprotected main. **Every repo, private included,** turns on auto-merge and branch deletion once it exists, on the owner's go (the gate prints the command; read back); with no required check the merge gate stays NO GO. Why: the first push sets the foundation; what it carries is public for good.
